content.code:
Every process has three streams:
  0: stdin  (standard input)  — where it reads data from
  1: stdout (standard output) — where normal output goes (usually screen)
  2: stderr (standard error)  — where error messages go (usually screen)

By default, both stdout and stderr appear in your terminal.
Redirection lets you send them to files or other commands.

# > redirects stdout to a file (OVERWRITES)
ls -la > filelist.txt       # save output to file
echo "Hello" > greeting.txt

# >> appends to a file (does not overwrite)
echo "line 1" > log.txt
echo "line 2" >> log.txt    # adds to log.txt

# 2> redirects stderr (errors) to a file
command 2> errors.log

# &> or 2>&1 redirects both stdout and stderr
command > output.log 2>&1         # both to same file
command &> output.log             # shorthand (bash)

# Discard output (/dev/null is a black hole)
command > /dev/null              # discard stdout
command 2> /dev/null             # discard errors
command > /dev/null 2>&1         # discard everything

# | sends stdout of left command to stdin of right command
ls -la | grep ".json"           # list only JSON files
cat access.log | grep "ERROR"   # same as: grep "ERROR" access.log
ps aux | grep nginx             # find nginx processes

# Chain multiple pipes
cat access.log | grep "404" | wc -l          # count 404 errors
ls -lS | head -10                            # 10 largest files
cat /etc/passwd | cut -d: -f1 | sort         # sorted list of users
history | grep "git" | tail -20              # last 20 git commands

# sort and uniq for frequency analysis
cat access.log | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10
# → top 10 IPs by request count

# xargs: pass stdin as arguments to a command
find . -name "*.log" | xargs rm          # delete found files
echo "file1 file2 file3" | xargs touch  # create multiple files

questions.question: You run: command > output.log 2>&1. What does this do?
options: Saves stdout to output.log and shows errors on screen
Saves both stdout and stderr to output.log
Saves stderr to output.log and discards stdout
questions.explanation: 2>&1 redirects stderr (file descriptor 2) to wherever stdout (file descriptor 1) currently points. Since stdout is already redirected to output.log, stderr also goes there. Order matters: write > output.log BEFORE 2>&1. The shorthand &> output.log does the same thing in bash.

faq.a: /dev/null is a special file that discards anything written to it and returns EOF when read. It is used to silence output: command > /dev/null discards stdout, 2>/dev/null discards errors. Useful in cron jobs and scripts where you want commands to run silently unless they fail.

examples: ps aux | grep nginx | grep -v grep — find running Nginx processes, excluding the grep process itself
cat access.log | awk '{print $9}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn — count HTTP status codes in a web server log
